source_text: Εἰς τοῦτο γὰρ ὑπέμεινεν ὁ κύριος παραδοῦναι τὴν σάρκα εἰς καταφθοράν, ἵνα τῇ ἀφέσει τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἁγνισθῶμεν, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ αἵματι τοῦ ῥαντίσματος αὐτοῦ. γέγραπται γὰρ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἅ μὲν πρὸς τὸν Ἰσραήλ, ἃ δὲ πρὸς ἡμᾶς, λέγει δὲ οὕτως: Ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν: τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν: ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἄφωνος ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτόν. οὐκοῦν ὑπερευχαριστεῖν ὀφείλομεν τῷ κυρίῳ, ὅτι καὶ τὰ παρεληλυθότα ἡμῖν ἐγνώρισεν καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἐνεστῶσιν ἡμᾶς ἐσόφισεν. καὶ εἰς τὰ μέλλοντα οὐκ ἐσμὲν ἀσύνετοι. λέγει δὲ ἡ γραφή: Οὐκ ἀδίκως ἐκτείνεται δίκτυα πτερωτοῖς. τοῦτο λέγει, ὅτι δικαίως ἀπολεῖται ἄνθρωπος, ὃς ἔχων ὁδοῦ δικαιοσύνης γνῶσιν ἑαυτὸν εἰς ὁδὸν σκότους ἀποσυνέχει. ἔτι δὲ καὶ τοῦτο, ἀδελφοί μου: εἰ ὁ κύριος ὑπέμεινεν παθεῖν περὶ τῆς ψυχῆς ἡμῶν, ὢν παντὸς τοῦ κόσμου κύριος ᾧ εἶπεν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου: Ποιήσωμεν ἄνθρωπον κατ’ εἰκόνα καὶ καθ̓ ὁμοίωσιν ἡμετέραν: πῶς οὖν ὑπέμεινεν ὑπὸ χειρὸς ἀνθρώπων παθεῖν; μάθετε. οἱ προφῆται, ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ ἔχοντες τὴν χάριν, εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπροφήτευσαν: αὐτὸς δέ, ἵνα καταργήσῃ τὸν θάνατον καὶ τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν ἀνάστασιν δείξῃ, ὅτι ὲν σαρκὶ ἕδει αὐτὸν φανερωθῆναι, ὑπέμεινεν, ἵνα τοῖς πατράσιν τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν ἀποδῷ, καὶ αὐτὸς ἑαυτῷ τὸν λαὸν τὸν καινὸν ἑτοιμάζων ἐπιδείξῃ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ὤν, ὅτι τὴν ἀνάστασιν αὐτὸς ποιήσας κρινεῖ. πέρας γέ τοι διδάσκων τὸν Ἰσραὴλ καὶ τηλικαῦτα τέρατα καὶ σημεῖα ποιῶν ἐκήρυσσεν, καὶ ὑπερηγάπησεν αὐτόν. ὅτε δὲ τοὺς ἰδίους ἀποστόλους τοὺς μέλλοντας κηρύσσειν τὸ εὐαγγέλιον αὐτοῦ ἐξελέξατο, ὄντας ὑπὲρ πᾶσαν ἁμαρτίαν ἀνομωτέρους, ἵνα δείξῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἦλθεν καλέσαι δικαίους, ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλούς, τότε ἐφανέρωσεν ἑαυτὸν εἶναι υἱὸν θεοῦ. εἰ γὰρ μὴ ἦλθεν ἐν σαρκί, οὐδ’ ἄν πως οἱ ἄνθρωποι ἐσώθησαν βλέποντες αὐτόν, ὅτε τὸν μέλλοντα μὴ εἶναι ἥλιον, ἔργου τῶν χειρῶν αὐτοῦ ὑπάρχοντα, ἐμβλέποντες οὐκ ἰσχύουσιν εἰς τὰς ἀκτῖνας αὐτοῦ ἀντοφθαλμῆσαι: οὐκοῦν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ εἰς τοῦτο ἐν σαρκὶ ἦλθεν, ἵνα τὸ τέλειον τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἀνακεφαλαιώσῃ τοῖς διώξασιν ἐν θανάτῳ τοὺς προφήτας αὐτοῦ. οὐκοῦν εἰς τοῦτο ὑπέμεινεν. λέγει γὰρ ὁ θεὸς τὴν πληγὴν τῆς σαρκὸς αὐτοῦ ὅτι ἐξ αὐτῶν: Ὅταν πατάξωσιν τὸν ποιμένα ἑαυτῶν, τότε ἀπολεῖται τὰ πρόβατα τῆς ποίμνης. αὐτὸς δὲ ἠθέλησεν οὕτω παθεῖν: ἔδει γάρ, ἵνα ἐπὶ ξύλου πάθῃ. λέγει γὰρ ὁ προφητεύων ἐπ’ αὐτῷ. Φεῖσαί μου τῆς ψυχῆς ἀπὸ ῥομφαίας, καί: Καθήλωσόν μου τὰς σάρκας, ὅτι πονηρευομένων συναγωγαὶ ἐπανέστησάν νέστησάν μοι. καὶ πάλιν λέγει: Ἰδού, τέθεικά μου τὸν νῶτον εἰς μάστιγας, τὰς δὲ σιαγόνας εἰς ῥαπίσματα. τὸ δὲ πρόσωπόν μου ἔθηκα ὡς στερεὰν πέτραν.
pass_a_gloss: For the Lord endured to deliver his flesh to destruction, so that by the forgiveness of sins we might be purified, which is in the blood of his sprinkling. For it is written about him, the things concerning Israel, and the things concerning us, and he says thus: He was wounded for our transgressions and bruised for our sins; by his stripe we were healed: as a sheep he was led to slaughter, and as a lamb silent before the one shearing him. Therefore we ought to give great thanks to the Lord, because he made known to us the things that have passed and in the present things he has made us wise, and we are not without understanding for the things to come. And the scripture says: The net is not spread in vain for the winged creatures. This it says, that justly a man will perish, who having the knowledge of the way of righteousness, binds himself to the way of darkness. And yet, my brothers, if the Lord endured to suffer for our soul, being Lord of all the world, to whom God said from the foundation of the world: Let us make man according to our image and likeness: how then did he endure to suffer by the hand of men? Learn. The prophets, having the gift from him, prophesied about him: and he, so that he might abolish death and show the resurrection from the dead, because it was necessary for him to be revealed in the flesh, endured, so that to the fathers he might give the promise, and he himself, preparing for himself a new people, might show on the earth, being, that he, having made the resurrection, will judge. For teaching the end to Israel and doing such great signs and wonders, he preached and loved him exceedingly. But when he chose his own apostles, who were going to preach his gospel, being more lawless than all sin, so that he might show that he did not come to call the righteous, but sinners, then he revealed himself to be the Son of God. For if he had not come in the flesh, men would not have been saved, seeing him, when they cannot even look at the sun, which is the work of his hands, because they are not able to gaze at its rays: therefore the Son of God came in the flesh, so that he might summarize the perfect things of sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. Therefore he endured. For God says the stroke of his flesh, that it is from them: When they strike their own shepherd, then the sheep of the flock will perish. But he himself willed to suffer thus: for it was necessary for him to suffer on the wood. For the prophet prophesying about him says: Spare my soul from the sword, and: Pierce my flesh, because the assemblies of the wicked rose up against me. And again he says: Behold, I have set my back for scourges, my cheeks for slaps. And my face I have set as a hard rock.

pass_b_english: The Lord endured handing over his flesh to corruption so that we might be cleansed by the forgiveness of sins through the blood of his sprinkling (Isaiah 53:5). Scripture speaks of him both to Israel and to us: he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities, and by his stripes we are healed; like a sheep he was led to the slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, he did not open his mouth (Isaiah 53:7). Because of this we owe the Lord overflowing thanks, for he has revealed the past to us, made us wise in the present, and given us understanding for the future. As Scripture says, 'The net is not spread in vain for the winged'—meaning that a person who knows the way of righteousness yet turns himself toward darkness justly perishes (Zechariah 13:7).

Brothers, consider: if the Lord endured suffering for our souls, even though he is Lord of all the world—to whom God said at the foundation of the world, 'Let us make man in our image and likeness'—how could he endure suffering at human hands? Learn this: the prophets, gifted by him, prophesied about him. He endured, so that he might abolish death and demonstrate the resurrection from the dead; it was necessary for him to be revealed in the flesh. He did this to fulfill the promise to the fathers and, while preparing a new people for himself on earth, to show that he, having brought about the resurrection, will judge. He taught Israel to the very end, performed such great signs and wonders, preached, and loved them exceedingly.

When he chose his own apostles—those who would proclaim his gospel—he picked men more lawless than any sinner, to prove that he came not to call the righteous but sinners. At that point he revealed himself as the Son of God. If he had not come in the flesh, no one could have been saved by seeing him; human beings cannot even stare at the sun, a mere work of his hands, because they cannot endure its rays. Therefore the Son of God came in the flesh to sum up the full measure of sins for those who persecuted his prophets to death. That is why he endured. God speaks of the stroke upon his flesh as coming from them: 'When they strike their shepherd, the sheep of the flock will perish' (Zechariah 13:7). Yet he himself willed to suffer this way, for it was necessary that he suffer on the wood. The prophet foretelling him says: 'Spare my soul from the sword'; 'Pierce my flesh, for assemblies of the wicked have risen against me.' And again: 'Behold, I have given my back to scourges and my cheeks to slaps; I have set my face like a flint.'

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that includes necessary scripture citations (Isaiah 53:5, Isaiah 53:7, Zechariah 13:7) which correspond correctly to the quoted/alluded Greek text. The translation of 'ὡς ἀμνὸς ἄφωνος ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος αὐτόν' as 'like a lamb silent before its shearer, he did not open his mouth' in Pass B is a valid expansion of the sense.
